proposal: The Mandate says the SEC and CFTC have handled digital assets mainly through enforcement and recommends a joint regulation under which a holder of a digital asset is not treated as party to an investment contract unless the holder is entitled to a share of enterprise earnings, a defined payment flow, or claims on assets in liquidation; otherwise the asset would be a CFTC-regulated commodity. It also recommends amending the statutory definitions of commodity and security, and, if regulators do not act, that Congress legislate.

status_summary: The agencies have moved in the same general direction through a joint interpretation and proposed rules, not the joint regulation and statutory definition changes the Mandate specifies. The SEC and CFTC issued a joint release labeled a final rule, interpretation and guidance (91 FR 13714), in which the SEC interprets the security definition and the CFTC provides guidance, published and effective 2026-03-23; it sorts crypto assets into five categories, says digital commodities, digital collectibles and digital tools are not securities in themselves (though they can be sold under an investment contract), describes when an investment contract ends, and states that the Howey test remains binding, so it does not adopt the Mandate's test based on entitlement to profits, payment flows or liquidation claims; the CFTC part says some non-security crypto assets could meet the Commodity Exchange Act definition of commodity. The SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets on 2026-08-21, with a $5 million four-year exemption, a $75 million annual exemption and a conditional safe harbor from the investment contract prong, with comments due 2026-10-20, and the CFTC published an advance notice on crypto asset transactions and markets on 2026-10-13, with comments due 2026-12-14. In Congress, the Senate rejected cloture 49-50 on 2026-09-15 (vote 234) on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, which Crypto Briefing reports passed the House 294-134 in July 2025, and the GENIUS Act (P.L. 119-27, 2025-07-18) covers payment stablecoins only.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14178, titled Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology, is signed (published in the Federal Register 2025-01-31).
The House passes H.R. 3633, 294-134, per Crypto Briefing (only the month, July 2025, is given, so the first of the month is used).
The GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, S. 1582), which provides for regulation of payment stablecoins, is approved.
The SEC and CFTC joint interpretation on the application of the federal securities laws to certain crypto assets is published in the Federal Register and takes effect the same day.
The SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets is published, with a tailored offering regime and a conditional safe harbor from the investment contract prong; comments are due 2026-10-20.
Senate vote 234: cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633 (digital commodity regulation by the SEC and CFTC) is rejected 49-50.

The CFTC publishes an advance notice of proposed rulemaking (91 FR 64811) seeking comment on rules implementing section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act for crypto asset transactions and markets (Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets); comments due 2026-12-14.
